newsitem.title: USA: Kerr-McGee sees Galatia down by 1 mln tons.
newsitem.headline: Kerr-McGee sees Galatia down by 1 mln tons.

text.p: Kerr-McGee Corp said Monday that production at its Galatia coal mine in southern Illinois could be down by as much as one million tons this year because of a suspension in mining.
The company said operations in one part of the Galatia mine was suspended last Tuesday because of elevated levels of carbon monoxide.
"We believe the high CO levels were caused by a burning of coal dust or methane gas," the company said in a statement.
The company said it met Monday with officials from the U.S. Mine Safety and Health Administration.
It said it is continuing mining operations in the unaffected areas, but believes production at Galatia this year could be hurt by as much as one million tons from the suspension.
The company said this would represent about three percent of its total 1997 coal production.
"We do not anticipate a reduction in work force at this time, and we are working with our customers to assure them of a steady supply of coal," a company statement said.
